abstract: New York Federal Reserve research finding that over 50% of firms in information and finance sectors report using AI, representing the highest sectoral adoption rates in the US economy. Despite this significant adoption, few firms report AI-related layoffs, suggesting that early AI integration is augmenting rather than displacing workers in these knowledge-intensive industries. The study provides central-bank-quality data on the gap between AI adoption and labor displacement.
keyFindings: Over 50% of firms in information and finance sectors report AI usage
Information and finance show the highest sectoral AI adoption rates
Few firms report AI-related layoffs despite significant adoption
Early evidence suggests augmentation rather than displacement in knowledge-intensive sectors
methodology: NY Fed survey of firms across sectors measuring AI adoption rates and associated workforce changes, with particular focus on information and financial services industries.
qualifiers: Firm-level self-reporting may undercount or overcount AI usage depending on definition. 'Few layoffs' does not rule out reduced hiring or slower headcount growth. Early adoption phase results may not predict longer-term employment effects as AI capabilities mature.
